overview: The committee recommended funding for five community preservation projects covering archaeological surveys, historical restorations, and park lighting. Members also reviewed the FY26 budget and finalized the 2026 meeting calendar with an emphasis on project tracking and public outreach.

items.title: Brooks Estate Archaeological Survey
items.summary: Recommended $10,000 for a desktop archaeological survey of the 57-acre Brooks Estate and cemetery parcel. Condition: project coordination with M-BELT and the cemetery trustees.

items.title: FY26 Budget Review
items.summary: Reviewed the funding availability for the fiscal year, confirming approximately $2.66 million in total assets against $2.58 million in proposed project allocations. The committee verified that sufficient reserves remain for off-cycle requests and small grants.

items.title: World War II Fountain Restoration
items.summary: Recommended $167,800 for the restoration of the Angel of Victory and Peace fountain. Condition: the city must provide a long-term maintenance plan.

items.title: Cross Street Cemetery Monument Restoration
items.summary: Recommended $126,500 for monument restoration and repairs to the perimeter wall at Cross Street Cemetery.

items.title: Shiloh Baptist Church Window Restoration Phase 2
items.summary: Recommended $150,000 for phase two of the stained glass window restoration. Conditions: identification of specific windows and submission of schematic drawings before disbursement; a motion to increase the grant amount by $35,000 was defeated.

items.title: Tufts Park Field Lighting Improvements
items.summary: Recommended $432,000 for upgraded lighting at Tufts Park Field 2. Conditions: future renovations must prioritize the retention and reuse of the new equipment or require repayment of the grant funds to the CPA reserve.

items.title: Application Process and 2026 Meeting Calendar
items.summary: Approved the 2026 meeting schedule and discussed improving the application process through earlier surveys and quarterly project updates. Members discussed increasing public engagement via park signage and tabling events.
